{"task": {"id": "I_kwDONElfw88AAAABXcHiMQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlV6PzhBAUQM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlV6P", "number": 74, "title": "Increase Bullet max substeps to 10 to reduce physics time loss during frame stalls", "body": "## Problem

The maintainer occasionally sees severe, persistent MMD physics instability and is testing **one isolated change at a time**. The remaining investigation item #2 is **lost simulated time on slow or stalled frames**.

Today [`src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts) uses `unitStep = 1/65`, **`maxStepNum = 3`** by default, and calls:

```ts
const maxStepNum = Math.min( Math.floor( delta / unitStep ) + 1, this.maxStepNum );
this.world!.stepSimulation( delta, maxStepNum, unitStep );
```

[Bullet's `btDiscreteDynamicsWorld::stepSimulation`](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/blob/master/src/BulletDynamics/Dynamics/btDiscreteDynamicsWorld.cpp) first consumes full fixed steps from its internal accumulator, **then clamps actual integrated steps to `maxSubSteps`**. The full requested step count is subtracted from its accumulator before this clamp, so excessive elapsed simulation time is discarded rather than kept for later catch-up. With a 100ms frame and `unitStep = 1/65`, at most three steps (~46ms) currently run even though approximately six or seven steps (~92–108ms, depending on residual fractional time) would be needed. The result can leave physics behind animated/kinematic bone inputs.

This is a real timekeeping limitation, **not proof** that dropped substeps cause the user's intermittent physics explosion.

A comparison of established MMD implementations motivates raising the bounded limit:

| Implementation | Default max substeps | Fixed step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| three-mmd-loader and legacy Three.js MMDPhysics | **3** | **1/65s** |
| [Saba](https://github.com/benikabocha/saba/blob/master/src/Saba/Model/MMD/MMDPhysics.cpp) | **10** | **1/120s** by default (configurable) |
| [babylon-mmd Bullet backend](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/main/src/Runtime/Optimized/Physics/Bind/Impl/physicsRuntime.ts) | **10** | **1/60s** by default (configurable) |

Both references continue using a **bounded** number of Bullet substeps, not unlimited recovery. Raising the limit increases CPU work on slow frames; it does not reconstruct earlier kinematic target poses between substeps, guarantee MikuMikuDance parity, or eliminate arbitrarily long stalls. The repository's public example [`examples/scene.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/examples/scene.ts) already caps the frame delta forwarded to `MMDAnimationHelper` to **0.1s**, for which 10 substeps is sufficient at the present 1/65 fixed step. Worker coalescing currently caps accumulated delta at 0.25s; larger backlog may still lose simulation time under a 10-step limit and is **not** addressed by this experiment.

## Expected outcome

Change the **default** `MMDPhysics.maxStepNum` from **3 to 10** to allow Bullet to integrate more elapsed time after frame drops while retaining bounded work per update. Keep `unitStep = 1/65` and the positive finite `delta` handling introduced by Issue #68 / PR #69. Do **not** force catch-up loops, change the animation clock or make the solver unbounded.

Preserve `params.maxStepNum` overrides: callers explicitly passing `3` or another supported value must retain that choice. Update relevant JSDoc/docs.

The change is a focused **physics-performance/stability experiment**. The maintainer will judge subsequent real-model behavior manually; do **not** add comparison toggles or require that subjective review before merge.

### Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Update the default `maxStepNum` from 3 to **10** in `src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts` and documented `MMDAnimationHelper.add(..., { maxStepNum })` default. Preserve `unitStep = 1/65`, explicit parameter overrides, the existing `Math.floor(delta / unitStep) + 1` per-call budget and Bullet's internal fractional-time accumulation. Keep this one behavioral change isolated.
- [ ] Use deterministic instrumentation of real Bullet/Ammo integration (not only `stepSimulation` argument assertions) for normal and slow-frame sequences: 30/60/120/144 FPS, approximately 20/10 FPS, a 100ms one-off stall and a stall exceeding the **10-substep** budget. Assert that substeps formerly dropped for typical <=100ms stalls now run, that simulation does **not** advance beyond elapsed time by more than numerical tolerance, and that very long stalls remain bounded rather than invoking unlimited catch-up.
- [ ] Preserve existing short-delta and zero/invalid-delta semantics from #68, including positive frames shorter than one fixed step sometimes completing zero Bullet substeps; verify that explicit `maxStepNum: 3` still retains the old bounded cap. Update existing tests that assert default 3.
- [ ] Exercise real PMD and PMX dynamic/kinematic constrained fixtures across standalone sync, shared sync and Worker-owned Bullet pathways, checking actual native trajectories / elapsed integration and consistent synchronization at supported boundaries. Cover Worker accumulated/batched deltas and its existing 0.25s coalescing policy without changing Worker queue/scheduling logic in this issue.
- [ ] Evaluate and document CPU work/step-count impact from a 100ms and larger stall. The new default may execute more substeps per frame; document this trade-off honestly, along with the limits of no intermediate kinematic animation poses. Do **not** assert that the user-reported violent oscillation is resolved, that no other regressions can occur, or that exact native MMD behavior is proven.
- [ ] Keep unrelated physics behaviors untouched: #70 additional damping, #72 linked-body collision policy, `STOP_ERP = 0.475`, rigid-body types/Type-2 sync, joints, IK, reset/warmup, gravity, recovery heuristics, rendering, materials and example lighting. No public UI or A/B switch.
- [ ] Run/report `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:examples`, relevant built-example/runtime checks and `git diff --check` on the PR branch. Technical validation and any real-model subjective assessment must be distinguished.
- [ ] **Do not make any check requiring the merged Pages site a pre-merge acceptance criterion or PR merge blocker.**

### Required post-merge verification

**After merge**, verify the merge-triggered GitHub Pages workflow successfully publishes the merge SHA. Verify the public PMD, Worker Physics and Gene Light PMX examples load without asset/runtime errors; record workflow URL, deployed commit/date and evidence. Mark these checks **PENDING** until completed. Track any deployment problem separately.

The maintainer's **optional post-merge real-model motion/stability evaluation** decides whether to keep or revert the increased default; it is **not a prerequisite for approval/merge**. Visual stability is not established by automated tests or Pages publication.

## Context

- Earlier experiment [#68](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/issues/68) / [PR #69](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/pull/69) correctly forwards positive short-frame deltas to Bullet and deliberately left the long-frame cap unchanged.
- Further isolated experiments [#70](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/issues/70) (additional damping) and [#72](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/issues/72) (linked-body collisions) are merged and should not be modified here.
- [Bullet time-step accumulation and clamp](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/blob/master/src/BulletDynamics/Dynamics/btDiscreteDynamicsWorld.cpp#L382-L449); [Saba defaults](https://github.com/benikabocha/saba/blob/master/src/Saba/Model/MMD/MMDPhysics.cpp); [babylon-mmd Bullet runtime defaults](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/main/src/Runtime/Optimized/Physics/Bind/Impl/physicsRuntime.ts).
- Potentially more sophisticated catch-up/clock synchronization policies are separate future investigations, not part of this narrowly scoped default-limit experiment.
